records.title_zh: 尼泊尔-西藏洪水：这就是面对气候危机不作为的代价
records.summary_source: Nepalis and Tibetans must not pay the price – with their lives, livelihoods and money meant for education and health – for global heating caused by wealthy states Sunil Acharya is an international climate policy and just transition specialist based in Kathmandu, Nepal As a Nepali citizen working on international climate policy for more than a decade, it is difficult to look at the harrowing images coming out of the catastrophic flash flood that thundered down valleys in Nepal, sweeping down the Lhende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, and not feel angry. Not just because of the destruction, but because it comes after years of warnings from scientists and civil society that a rapidly warming planet would make disasters more frequent, more intense and harder to predict. This is what the cost of delaying global climate action looks like. records.title_original: Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn
records.title_zh: 专家警告：气候危机可能正在破坏尼泊尔等山区的不稳定性
records.summary_source: Unusual heat this year may have melted ice and thawed bonds that hold glaciers in place – leading to catastrophe Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates What caused the flash flood in Nepal and Tibet? The devastating flash flood that has ripped through the border communities of Nepal and Tibet has heightened fears that the climate crisis is destabilising the geology of mountain and polar regions, threatening millions of people. Satellite imagery suggests a glacier collapse high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the deadly torrent of mud, water and ice that tore along the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday. It swept away buildings and roads and left at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 尼泊尔与西藏边境地区发生毁灭性山洪，造成至少 360 人死亡、1400 人失踪。卫星图像与地震波分析显示，喜马拉雅山脉发生的冰川崩塌及随后的冰石雪崩是导致这场灾难的主因。科学家指出，今年异常的高温融化了冰层并削弱了固定冰川的岩石结合力，加剧了全球山区地质的不稳定性。
records.why_zh: 凸显了全球气候变暖对高山及极地冰川地质稳定性的直接威胁，对区域防灾减灾与气候适应政策具有重要参考意义。事实表明冰川崩塌引发了山洪，专家将其归因于全球变暖引起的高温。

records.title_original: More than 380 coastal World Heritage Sites may face climate risks, new data shows
records.title_zh: 新数据显示，逾 380 处沿海世界遗产地可能面临气候风险
records.summary_source: - Coral reefs, medieval coastal castles and mangrove forests on UNESCO’s World Heritage list now share something in common: Precise digital boundaries. - A new dataset maps 386 coastal World Heritage Sites, offering the clearest picture yet of what stands to be lost as the world’s climate changes. - Covering 235 million hectares (~581 million acres) of coastline, the new high-resolution, open-access dataset can be used by researchers and local managers to study flooding, erosion and other climate risks faced by heritage sites. - The tool is a critical first step to understand climate risks, but not a substitute for the local knowledge needed to help these places survive, some experts say.
records.summary_zh: 一项最新发布的高分辨率开源数据集详细绘制了全球 386 处沿海世界遗产地的精确数字化边界。这些覆盖 2.35 亿公顷海岸线的遗址涵盖珊瑚礁、城堡与红树林等自然和文化地标，正面临洪水、侵蚀等气候变化威胁，可为研究人员与地方管理者评估脆弱性提供重要工具。
records.why_zh: 该数据集首次为全球沿海世界遗产地提供了统一的高分辨率数字化边界，填补了地方气候脆弱性评估工具的空白，具有重要的适应政策支撑意义。此处属于基于科学研究的客观事实界定。

records.title_original: El Niño climate patterns supercharged by burning of fossil fuels, study finds
records.title_zh: 研究发现：化石燃料燃烧使厄尔尼诺气候模式进一步加剧
records.summary_source: ‘Godzilla’ event currently brewing could push 50 million people into acute hunger before the end of next year A series of strong El Niño climatic patterns in recent decades, such as the “Godzilla” event currently brewing that is set to warp weather around the world, have been supercharged by the broader overheating of the planet caused by the burning of fossil fuels, a major new study has found. El Niño is a naturally occurring phenomenon, taking place every two to seven years, when the waters of the eastern tropical Pacific Ocean heat up, causing a cascade of impacts around the world. The latest developing El Niño, set to peak later this year, is set to be the strongest in living memory and has been informally dubbed a “Godzilla” event. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 一项最新研究发现，近几十年来一系列强烈的厄尔尼诺气候模式受到了化石燃料燃烧引发的全球变暖的显著加剧。科学家通过分析加拉帕戈斯群岛的珊瑚化石发现，人类造成的全球变暖不仅会因厄尔尼诺现象而放大，反过来也使厄尔尼诺现象本身变得更加强烈，这对全球气候灾害和脆弱人群构成了严重威胁。
records.why_zh: 该研究从科学机理上阐明了化石燃料燃烧与极端厄尔尼诺事件之间的正反馈循环，为全球气候谈判中的减排承诺提供了基于长期珊瑚记录的实证支撑。事实表明温室气体正在改变自然气候循环，但具体影响程度仍取决于未来排放路径。

But the rising risks from shrinking glaciers must be faced too Thousands of people in Nepal and Tibet are in desperate need of emergency assistance following Wednesday’s disaster. With 360 people confirmed dead, more than 1,300 others are still missing as search and rescue operations continue. The precise sequence of events linking glacier collapse to flash floods is yet to be confirmed. But there is no doubting the enormous destructive power of the brown torrent that can be seen on video clips surging down the steeply sided Himalayan valleys, sweeping away everyone and everything in its path. Testimony from survivors about terrifying near-escapes and losses is reminiscent of previous disasters, including the 2004 tsunami. With some of the worst-affected areas still cut off and accessible only by helicopter, there is a high level of uncertainty about the total number of people who have died or homes that have been destroyed. records.summary_source: Reform and the Conservatives are willing to mislead the public, but as environment secretary, I believe we must be honest – and act boldly This long, hot summer has brought our third drought in five years and the driest July in almost two centuries . We’ve seen wildfires burn down homes and now face the risk of flash floods as we move into autumn. It should be a wake-up call for those saying that concerns about the climate crisis are overblown; that we should simply sit back and do nothing; or row back on attempts to restore our natural environment. records.summary_source: ONS data shows rising toll of climate crisis, with officials warning this summer on track to set further records More than 40,000 extra people died on the hottest days in England between 1988 and 2025 than would be expected in normal temperatures, according to data published by the Office for National Statistics on Wednesday. The figures do not include this summer, when England has sweltered under a succession of heatwaves and is on track to record its highest ever number of heat-related deaths . The UK Health Security Agency announced on 30 July that an estimated 2,877 people had died in the May and June heatwaves alone. The total is almost double the figure for the whole summer in 2025. records.why_zh: 该数据揭示了气候危机对公共健康的长期致命影响，凸显出英国亟需加强高温适应与医疗应急政策。事实层面明确了历史超额死亡人数与近期热浪数据，边界清晰指向英格兰及威尔士地区。

records.summary_source: - A 10-year agreement provides York Timber Holdings with access to renewable electricity “at scale,” an official with the timber company said. - The agreement will reduce the sawmill’s greenhouse gas emissions, while reducing its exposure to electricity tariff hikes and potential future carbon-based costs, according to the company. - “Renewable energy is just one element of sustainability. records.title_original: Indigenous water systems gain ground as climate pressures intensify in Bolivia
records.title_zh: 随着气候压力在玻利维亚加剧，土著水利系统取得进展
records.summary_source: - When a 2022 drought hit Bolivia’s Ascensión de Guarayos, restoring traditional paúros helped the community survive after the municipal reservoir ran dry. - The youth-led effort to revive paúros has grown into a broader conservation project, including a legally protected urban ecological corridor. - The initiative is part of a global trend to restore Indigenous water systems as low-cost, climate-resilient solutions to growing water scarcity. - Experts say blending traditional and modern approaches can strengthen water security — but only if local communities lead and retain control.
records.summary_zh: 2022年玻利维亚发生严重干旱、市政水库枯竭时，阿森西奥-德瓜拉约斯的青年通过恢复传统的 paúros 泉水池帮助社区渡过难关。这一青年主导的修复行动已发展成为更广泛的保护项目，成为应对全球水资源短缺的低成本气候韧性解决方案。

records.title_original: ‘132F’: meet the man calling out NYC’s infernally hot subway stations
records.title_zh: “132华氏度”：认识这位呼吁关注纽约市酷热地铁站的人
records.summary_source: Jack Klein takes heat readings, gives fans to overheated passengers and lugs big jugs of water into the stations On a recent August day in the subterranean furnace of New York City ’s subway, one bearded, curly-haired man was studying his phone for different reasons than the other wilting passengers – to track the soaring temperatures and ponder how underground train stations can cool down in an era of climate crisis . Jack Klein, a 31-year-old construction site manager, has in the past two years taken it upon himself to become a sort of guerrilla subway heat operative, sticking teardrop-shaped thermometers to steel beams in seven of the hottest Manhattan stations and posting social media videos of the hades-like summer temperatures that commuters have to endure. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 在纽约市闷热的地铁站内，31岁的建筑工地经理杰克·克莱恩自发监测气温，记录曼哈顿最热车站内高达132华氏度的体感温度，并向乘客提供水和风扇。这一极端高温现象对维护工人和乘客构成了严重的健康威胁，凸显出气候危机下城市地下交通系统亟需降温改造。
records.why_zh: 该报道揭示了气候危机下城市公共交通基础设施在极端高温应对方面的脆弱性，事实表明地下地铁站点的体感温度极高并威胁工人和乘客健康，这对城市气候适应政策和公共卫生防御具有现实警示意义。

records.title_zh: REDD+ 能否为菲律宾伊拉亚·曼扬人带来福祉？
records.summary_source: - The Mindoro Forest and Biodiversity Conservation Programme combines Indigenous forest patrols, ancestral-domain support, carbon monitoring and livelihood projects to protect more than 40,000 hectares (nearly 99,000 acres) of Iraya Mangyan forest. - Indigenous patrollers and local officials say the program has already strengthened monitoring and helped reduce timber poaching and small-scale mining, while surveys have documented hundreds of plant and animal species across the project area. - Community nurseries and paid conservation roles are creating early livelihood opportunities, but many benefits remain limited and uneven while the project awaits verification, a finalized benefit-sharing agreement and carbon revenue expected no earlier than around 2029. - Whether the program can deliver lasting benefits will depend on finalizing a transparent revenue-sharing agreement, sustaining patrols and livelihoods during the long wait for carbon income, and ensuring the Iraya retain a meaningful role in decisions over their forests.

records.summary_source: There are countless initiatives around the world that can inspire people and spur them into action. Amid the devastation of the climate crisis, our journalists strive to highlight these stories of hope Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support The news is very often about the bad things (especially if you’re on the Guardian’s environment desk). Wildfires, floods, tipping points, billionaires making huge profits and buying themselves island refuges for the apocalypse … And yet, ticking along beside that is the steady pulse of what the rest of humanity is doing in response to the climate crisis. From housing developments with no cars to buildings made out of hemp, all over the planet people are ploughing ahead and changing their neighbourhoods and cities and the world. But as news stories typically need to be about new developments or things people didn’t previously know about, it can be hard to cover all those brilliant initiatives being undertaken in the background – no matter how cheering they are. records.summary_source: - While emergency responders prioritized human life and property during Australia’s 2019-2020 Black Summer bushfires, there were few systems in place to protect wildlife or evacuate and care for domestic animals during and after the fires, exposing a gap in disaster planning. - Neighbors, wildlife carers, veterinarians, landholders and volunteers rapidly organized evacuations, rescue efforts, feeding stations and supply networks, demonstrating the power of local knowledge and grassroots coordination. - Fire ecology research suggests animals may be more vulnerable to fire than previously understood, and more research is needed to understand wildlife mortality and survival during and post-bushfire. - Experts say that community-led efforts could dramatically improve outcomes for both people and animals during disasters with better funding, coordination and institutional support. records.title_zh: 关于亚洲热浪及其健康影响需要了解的六件事
records.summary_source: - This year’s extreme weather has been linked to El Niño, which, according to weather experts, could be one of the strongest ever recorded. - Record-breaking temperatures were recorded in South Korea and Hong Kong, and mercury exceeded 40°C in Japan and China. - Apart from heatstroke risks, higher temperatures during El Niño can accelerate the life cycle of Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit dengue, and shorten the time for the virus to replicate, experts warn.
records.summary_zh: 受史上最强厄尔尼诺现象及人为气候变化共同影响，亚洲多地近期遭遇创纪录热浪。韩国、日本、中国及中国香港等地气温纷纷突破 40℃，韩国阳山更录得 42.5℃高温。专家警告，极端高温不仅导致中暑和死亡风险上升，还会加速登革热病毒传播媒介伊蚊的生命周期并缩短病毒复制时间。

records.title_original: Proposed London datacentre ‘incompatible’ with net zero with 1m-tonne carbon footprint
records.title_zh: 拟建的伦敦数据中心碳足迹达100万吨，与净零目标“不相容”
records.summary_source: Exclusive: Planning documents show annual emissions from North Ockendon project would be equivalent to 8,480 flights to New York A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 8,480 flights from London to New York, planning documents show. The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 规划文件显示，位于伦敦外围的东黑弗灵数据中心园区每年将产生超过100万吨二氧化碳，其全生命周期60年内预计产生超7200万吨二氧化碳当量。该项目由Digital Reef开发，占地218公顷绿化带，全面运营后预计每年耗电26.5亿千瓦时，对英国的脱碳进程构成重大威胁。
records.why_zh: 该项目凸显了人工智能与云计算驱动下大型数据中心激增对国家电网和净零目标的严峻挑战。报道反映的事实表明高能耗数字基础设施与长期减排路径存在显著冲突。

records.summary_zh: 今年夏天欧洲遭遇创纪录热浪与干旱，导致风力发电受阻，核电、燃气和煤电等热电厂因冷却水短缺被迫减产。相比之下，太阳能发电表现超常，结合电池储能满足了历史性高温下的空调电力需求，为欧洲气候适应能源系统提供了关键经验。

records.summary_source: Researchers are beginning to untangle how the “drought-disease paradox” works.
records.summary_zh: 最新研究表明，随着全球气候变暖和多地持续干旱，所谓的“干旱-疾病悖论”正导致霍乱、西尼罗河病毒和登革热等部分传染病和寄生虫意外爆发。尽管许多水生病原体需要水分，但在水体减少的情况下，部分致命感染与媒介反而通过集聚或生态变化加速了传播。
records.why_zh: 该研究探讨了干旱与传染病传播之间反直觉的联系，具有评估气候变化次生公共卫生风险的学术与政策意义。事实表明干旱不一定会抑制所有病原体，部分水媒及蚊媒传染病反而在干旱中滋生。

records.summary_zh: 德国波茨坦气候影响研究所发布的一项研究显示，在高排放情景下，受持续的高温、干旱和风力天气驱动，到本世纪末气候变化可能使欧洲野火过火面积增加近三倍。低排放情景下过火面积预计增加约39%，高排放情景下则可能高达192%。研究人员指出，随着极端天气加剧，即使升温幅度相对较小，地中海及西欧和中欧地区也将面临更频繁的野火威胁，消防能力或将接近极限。

records.summary_zh: 中国新发布的煤炭行业规划强调能源安全与绿色低碳转型，但未明确设定煤炭消费量达峰或削减的时间表。专家意见存在分歧，部分观点认为该规划旨在到2030年前稳定而非积极削减煤炭消费，并对继续发展煤炭化学工业表示关切；另有观点则认为，受房地产低迷、工业用煤减少及煤炭进口下降等因素影响，中国的煤炭消费可能已经达峰或将在今年至明年的短时间内实现达峰。

records.summary_zh: 英国反对党保守党在一份新报告中主张放弃 2050 年净零排放目标，并声称通过采用更多天然气和核能来替代可再生能源可节省超过 3200 亿英镑。然而，专家指出该报告的建模和假设存在严重漏洞，其实际替代方案不仅会导致减排力度大减，还会增加数亿吨二氧化碳排放，且无法带来最低的总成本。

records.title_original: Without action wildfires in Europe will increase 39% even in best-case climate scenario, study finds
records.title_zh: 研究发现：即便在最佳气候情景下，若不采取行动，欧洲野火也将增加39%
records.summary_source: Improvements in fire management however could mitigate increases by more than 70%, study shows Wildfires are projected to burn 39% more of Europe by the end of the century even in the best-case scenario for stopping the planet from heating, a study has found , unless action is taken to manage them better. The increase in hot, dry and windy weather that leads to small fires turning into raging infernos is to engulf more of Europe as carbon pollution pushes temperatures higher. In the worst-case scenario the researchers modelled, which would see global heating reach 3.6C above preindustrial levels, the burnt area would almost triple. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 一项研究发现，到本世纪末，即便在阻止地球变暖的最佳情景下，欧洲野火焚烧面积仍将增加39%。如果全球升温达到工业化前水平的3.6度这一最坏情景，过火面积将几乎翻倍。研究同时显示，改善消防管理能够将火灾增加幅度缓解70%以上，但无法完全消除影响。
records.why_zh: 该研究量化了不同温升情景对欧洲野火过火面积的影响，凸显了气候减排与消防管理并重的重要性，对欧洲适应气候变化及灾害管理政策具有参考价值。

records.title_original: Climate change drove extreme July heat in European seas, study finds
records.title_zh: 研究发现气候变化导致欧洲海域七月极端高温
records.summary_source: European coastal waters recorded unprecedented sea surface temperatures in July 2026. A new study has found that human-induced climate change primarily drove the temperature surge, pushing marine ecosystems past their limits. The rapid analysis was conducted by World Weather Attribution (WWA), a global network of researchers who analyze the influence of climate change in extreme […]
records.summary_zh: 世界天气归因组织的一项最新研究显示，2026 年 7 月欧洲沿岸海域记录到前所未有的海面温度，人类活动引起的气候变化是导致此次极端高温的主要原因。研究表明，在化石燃料燃烧驱动的全球变暖影响下，凯尔特海、比斯开湾及地中海等区域的海温较历史基准偏高 2.4 摄氏度，如果没有人为全球变暖，这种极端高温几乎不可能发生。
records.why_zh: 该研究通过归因分析定量证实了化石燃料燃烧对欧洲近海海洋热浪的直接推动作用，对评估海洋生态系统临界点及制定区域气候适应政策具有重要科学参考意义。

records.title_original: Weatherwatch: Climate crisis fuelling steep fall in migratory bird numbers
records.title_zh: 气象观察：气候危机加剧候鸟数量急剧下降
records.summary_source: Many species under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the planet’s largest mass-migration systems It may still feel like summer, but in the world of birds, autumn migration is already well under way. Cuckoos and swifts have already left us, and while swallows and many species of warbler will not depart our shores until September, many species of Arctic-breeding waders have begun to stop off at our coastal marshes to refuel for their long journey south. This year, however, there could be fewer than usual. A review by the British Trust for Ornithology, working with other international conservation organisations, has found that more than half of these global travellers are suffering major declines in numbers – a worrying downward trend. Many of those under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the largest mass-migration systems on the planet. Continue reading...

records.summary_source: Regulations that would block sale of older tires praised by environmental groups amid rightwing backlash California has become the first state in the nation to mandate that replacement tires be energy efficient, a major auto industry regulation set to block the sale of older tires and make vehicles on the road greener. State regulators have said the new rules will reduce emissions and drivers’ fuel costs. But the rules – which come as the Trump administration fights to block other California restrictions to promote greener cars – have already sparked a rightwing backlash, with one conservative news outlet calling the policies a “massive overreach”. records.summary_source: New research suggests a “massive and untapped” opportunity for conservation within commercial concessions in Southeast Asia, reports Mongabay’s Carolyn Cowan. Using satellite data, researchers identified roughly 42 million hectares (104 million acres) of intact forest still standing inside logging, timber, rubber and oil palm concessions across Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Myanmar. The study suggests that […]
records.summary_zh: 新研究表明，东南亚商业特许经营区内仍保存有约 4200 万公顷的完整森林，清除这些森林可能在未来 30 年内释放 12 亿吨二氧化碳。研究指出，按当前每吨 5 至 12 美元的碳价，仅依靠碳市场激励特许经营商保护森林在经济上并不可行，需要辅以绿色金融和生态系统服务付费等更广泛的融资组合。
records.why_zh: 该研究指出了当前自愿碳市场价格偏低对东南亚森林保护的局限性，对气候资金与区域生物多样性政策具有参考意义，体现了学术界对政策工具局限性的评估。

records.title_original: Carbon pollution has fuelled ‘massive expansion’ of marine heatwaves in Europe, study finds
records.title_zh: 研究发现碳污染导致欧洲海洋热浪“大规模扩张”
records.summary_source: Hottest periods this year in most sea regions would have been ‘virtually impossible’ in a preindustrial climate Carbon pollution has fuelled a “massive expansion” of marine heatwaves in Europe this summer, research has found, with some waters recording temperatures 6C higher than normal. The hottest fortnights of this year would have been “virtually impossible” in a preindustrial climate in three of the four sea regions studied, according to analysis by World Weather Attribution , while in the Celtic region, which covers much of the water around the British Isles, heat hit levels that used to strike just once a century. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 世界天气归因分析组织研究发现，碳污染导致欧洲今夏海洋热浪“大规模扩张”，部分海域水温较正常水平高出6摄氏度。在所研究的四个海域中，有三个海域今年最热的两周在前工业化气候条件下几乎不可能发生，气候崩塌导致了约三分之二的过量热量，对海洋生态系统和沿海地区构成严重威胁。
records.why_zh: 该研究通过归因分析量化了化石燃料燃烧对欧洲海温异常的具体影响，凸显了海洋变暖对沿海及生态系统的长期气候风险，为欧盟区域气候适应政策提供了科学依据（基于观测数据与模型模拟的科学事实，不涉及谈判博弈）。

records.title_original: On the Great Barrier Reef, management by Traditional Owners is growing
records.title_zh: 在大堡礁，传统所有者的管理作用正在增强
records.summary_source: - Joint management of the Great Barrier Reef is changing, with Traditional Owners playing an increasing role in the conservation of one of the seven natural wonders of the world. - Despite climate change continuing to threaten the health of the Reef, the World Heritage Committee has again decided not to put the Great Barrier Reef on its “in danger” list, and has cited increased levels of Traditional Owner management in its decision. - Traditional use and management agreements currently cover 43% of the Great Barrier Reef’s coastline and the government has announced new funding and measures to further include Indigenous management. - There are still gaps in the full inclusion of Indigenous communities in the stewardship of their traditional waters, say Indigenous governance organizations, though strides are being made.
records.summary_zh: 澳大利亚大堡礁的共同管理模式正在发生变化，传统所有者在保护这一世界自然遗产方面发挥着日益重要的作用。尽管气候持续对大堡礁健康构成威胁，但世界遗产委员会再次决定不将其列入“濒危”名单，并在决策中提及了传统所有者管理水平的提高。目前，传统使用和管理协议已覆盖大堡礁43%的海岸线，政府也宣布了新的资金和措施以进一步纳入土著管理。
records.why_zh: 该报道展示了传统所有者参与大堡礁治理对国际保护名录决策的积极影响，突显了扩大土著管理范围在应对气候威胁与世界遗产保护中的政策意义。事实表明土著管理协议已覆盖43%海岸线，世界遗产委员会因此未将其列入濒危名单。

records.summary_source: The world is currently experiencing what is expected to become the strongest El Niño on record – dubbed a “super El Niño”… The post Explainer: How the ‘super El Niño’ will reshape the world’s weather appeared first on Carbon Brief .

records.why_zh: 该文梳理了厄尔尼诺南方涛动（ENSO）周期的运行机制及其对全球气温和极端天气的影响，属于对气候科学事实的客观解释。

records.summary_source: - In Paraty, Brazil, a Caiçara family has transformed seaweed cultivation into gastronomy, educational tourism and a source of income. The venture is driven by strong female participation and a deep connection to their territory. - Originally introduced in Brazil to supply the carrageenan industry, the macroalgae Kappaphycus alvarezii is also being used as a biofertilizer and increasingly as a food item.. - Its farming also supports ecological balance. It produces oxygen, absorbs carbon and helps improve water quality by filtering out excess nutrients. - Experts say the expansion of seaweed farming in Brazil faces bottlenecks in credit, marketing, technology and regulation. New research networks and public policies are attempting to organize the sector as part of the country’s growing bioeconomy.
records.summary_zh: 在巴西帕拉蒂，一个凯萨拉家庭将海藻种植转化为餐饮、教育旅游和收入来源。源自菲律宾的大藻卡帕藻最初引入巴西是为了供应卡拉胶产业，如今也被用作生物肥料和食品。海藻种植能产生氧气、吸收碳并通过过滤多余营养改善水质，但专家指出其发展仍面临信贷、营销、技术和监管瓶颈。

records.title_original: How soon will the drought be over?
records.title_zh: 干旱何时才能结束？
records.summary_source: Rain has returned to parts of the UK this week but is it enough to end the drought some regions are facing?
records.summary_zh: 英国部分地区本周迎来降雨，引发公众关于旱情何时结束的疑问。科学家指出，短期降雨无法彻底解除干旱，水资源完全恢复需要河流水位、土壤水分以及地下水和水库储量经历数月的持续补给。气象、土壤及河流干旱已相继显现，但由于地下水和水库尚未陷入严重枯竭，专家预计需等待秋冬降雨及明年春季的水文评估来判断旱情走向。

records.summary_source: Woodland Trust says trees struggling in drought stress, with older ‘survivors’ disproportionately affected England’s ancient oak trees are dying in the summer’s extreme heat and dry weather, according to the Woodland Trust, with trees and ecosystems unable to adapt fast enough to the changing climate. The heatwaves across much of Europe this summer have had a notable impact on crop growth and plant health. To cope with the extreme conditions, many trees are undergoing “early autumn”, wilting and losing their leaves early. Crow Leasow oak, Shropshire. Tea Party oak, Suffolk. King John oak, Devon. Enmore oak, Somerset. Lydham Manor oak, Shropshire. Old Knobbley, Essex. Pwllpriddog oak, Carmarthenshire. Continue reading...

records.summary_zh: 美国第二大水库于周六创下历史最低水位，几天前该国最大的水库也打破了自身的纪录。米德湖和鲍威尔湖均位于科罗拉多河上，为美国西南部七个州的约 4000 万人口以及约 55 万英亩农田提供城市用水。专家指出，气候变化、人口增长和过度消耗是导致水位降至历史新低的主要原因。

records.summary_source: Vegetable and grain growers call for urgent action, warning of ‘catastrophic’ harvests due to continent-wide drought Successive intense heatwaves and an increasingly severe, continent-wide drought have left many of Europe’s farmers in an “unprecedented” crisis, with vegetable and grain growers in particular warning of “catastrophic” harvests. French vegetable production is down by “a very significant extent” compared with previous years, French growers have said, with shortfalls put at 25% for courgettes, 35% for lettuces, 40% for peas, 60% for broccoli and 50% to 100% for artichokes. Continue reading...

records.title_original: Ithaca: a scintillating eco-thriller RPG that aims to confront our violent moment
records.title_zh: 《伊萨卡》：一款旨在直面我们暴力时代的精彩生态惊悚RPG游戏
records.summary_source: The latest game from ‘reality-inspired’ studio the Pixel Hunt sees you transporting precious human cargo – and deciding what to do with it Ithaca has one hell of an opening: Penelope, a disillusioned environmental lawyer, stops her car at a petrol station. But upon returning, she discovers something shocking: the unconscious body of an oil company CEO in her boot, his hands hog-tied together, dangling limply towards the vehicle’s number plate. This tantalising eco-thriller setup is a long way off the typical knights-and-castles fantasy fare of most role-playing games, more How To Blow Up a Pipeline than Dragon Quest . But road-trip RPG Ithaca arrives via refreshingly original developer the Pixel Hunt, a French outfit that specialises in what it calls “reality-inspired” games. The studio has made a number of arresting works in recent years. One was about a Syrian refugee couple making a perilous migrant journey across Europe; another tackled the life-shattering effects of child sexual abuse. The climate crisis was always in the back of Pixel Hunt founder and Ithaca writer Florent Maurin’s mind. After all, he says, it is the uber problem of our day, the problem that touches all other
records.summary_zh: 法国游戏工作室 The Pixel Hunt 推出了现实主义生态惊悚 RPG 游戏《伊萨卡》。游戏讲述了一位环保律师发现汽车后备箱里绑着一名石油公司首席执行官，玩家需要在游戏中做出涉及气候危机与道德抉择的剧情路线决策。
records.why_zh: 反映了气候危机作为时代议题正进一步向文化创意和游戏产业渗透，通过艺术形式探讨环境伦理与抗争边界。该内容属于文化产品与社会意识形态范畴，不直接构成气候外交谈判事实。

records.summary_source: Extreme weather has raised the significance of Cop17 talks starting this week on tackling drought and land degradation As swathes of the northern hemisphere bake in what could be the hottest year on record, with wildfires blazing across North America and Europe and heatwaves afflicting millions across Asia, the UN’s bi-annual talks on desertification have assumed much greater importance – and have started attracting more money. records.summary_source: As wildfires rage across Europe and Britain swelters through its hottest summer on record, literary fiction has a vital role to play in capturing the severe consequences of climate crisis Earlier this summer, I travelled through Europe on a book tour. Everywhere I went, the heat broke records. In Italy, Germany and Spain, I sought refuge from the afternoon sun in air-conditioned hotels. In normally temperate Zurich, it averaged 37 degrees. I jumped into the Limmat for relief. On my final day in Warsaw, Poland had never been hotter – one of 14 countries to hit a historic high. In June, when I left to return to the US, Europe was scorching. At the end of July, as I write this, it is burning. Since the heatwaves began, there have been more than 10,000 excess deaths. Yet for many, myself included, the high temperatures brought nothing more than inconvenience – uncomfortable commutes, heat rash, less time outdoors. This seems to be a defining feature of today’s climate crisis; deadly for some, banal for others. Even when the world is on fire, it somehow doesn’t feel like an emergency for everyone. records.summary_source: The Guardian travelled 100 miles along the EU’s longest river, where some residents are struggling to secure drinking water For centuries, the rock was seen as a warning. When it began to emerge from the Danube, beneath Gellért Hill in Budapest, it meant the river had fallen so low that floating mills could no longer operate, crops were probably failing, and hunger would almost certainly follow. That is why, in the Hungarian capital, where over time the boulder became little more than a legend, it was named Ínség-szikla – the Rock of Starvation. Today, amid record-low water levels on the Danube, the rock has not only emerged from the water, but surfaced almost in its entirety, along with the sandy riverbed on which it rests, astonishing geologists and government scientists sent to examine it. And, much as the rock was said to warn, Hungary is now facing an unprecedented energy crisis that has forced the country to shut down all but one of its Danube-cooled nuclear reactors for the first time in 44 years. records.title_zh: 从旅游业到发电和生产力，欧洲切实承受着热浪带来的经济成本
records.summary_source: Low river levels have stalled German freight traffic and forced closure of nuclear plants in France Across Europe this scorching summer, workers have struggled in the heat as wildfires raged and critical infrastructure was shut down. Here we look at the impact of the heatwaves on several major economies across mainland Europe – with the help of analysis from economists at the Dutch bank Triodos , who estimate a total of €180bn could be wiped off EU GDP by the heatwaves. In the UK, the green thinktank Verdant said this week that the heat had already cost the economy £4.4bn by the end of July. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 今年夏季欧洲多地遭遇酷暑，低水位导致德国货运受阻，法国核电站被迫关闭。荷兰特里多斯银行经济学家估计，极端热浪可能导致欧盟国内生产总值减少1800亿欧元。英国绿色智库“青翠”则表示，截至7月底，酷暑已给英国经济造成44亿英镑的损失，气温超过30摄氏度时劳动生产率往往会出现下降。

records.title_original: Fire rangers of Mongolian steppe: climate crisis spurs revival of ancient knowledge – photo essay
records.title_zh: 蒙古草原的消防员：气候危机促使人们重新发掘古代智慧——图片报道
records.summary_source: Fire has always be part of life on the grasslands, but has grown worse due to rising temperatures and severe droughts. In response, people have turned to their nomadic heritage to help tackle the blazes Sodnomjamts Damchaabadgar squats in a shallow, rocky depression, working quietly with his hands. Inches above the rim of the pit, the wind whips across the grasslands. But in the marginal shelter of the dig site the air remains calm – essential for delicate operations. Damchaabadgar, a research fellow at the Institute of Archaeology at the Mongolian Academy of Sciences, has erected a ger, a traditional nomad’s tent, nearby, which serves as his sleeping quarters and a field station. Two gers stand alone against the vast openness of the steppe in Eastern Mongolia. The ger – often called a yurt outside Mongolia – is a round dwelling designed to be assembled or disassembled in a matter of hours Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 由于气温上升和严重干旱，蒙古草原上的野火问题日益恶化。面对这一威胁，当地民众开始利用游牧传统遗产来协助扑灭大火，其中包括研究人员在东部草原搭建传统蒙古包开展野外工作，并结合考古发现探讨古代蒙古人如何利用驯马速度应对草原自然威胁。
records.why_zh: 该报道展示了气候变暖加剧欧亚草原野火频发的严峻事实，并记录了当地将游牧传统与科学调查相结合的应对实践，反映出事实层面的气候适应需求。

records.title_original: Alarmed by the alarm: people react to ‘severe alert’ on phones over UK wildfires
records.title_zh: 对警报感到警惕：英国野火手机“严重警报”引发民众反应
records.summary_source: Many complained online that piercingly loud tone was ‘overreach’ while others lamented lack of action on decarbonisation On Friday at 7pm, Thérèse Coffey was nine miles away from a nuclear power station when her phone made a loud, piercing and very worrying sound: it was a “severe” emergency alert . “Was expecting [a] much more specific alert, not a generic message on wildfires,” the former Conservative cabinet minister said on X. She wasn’t alone in being alarmed by the alarm sent to phones in England and Wales. In the aftermath, thousands of social media users expressed their shock at the alert. Some shared funny memes and others lamented what they viewed as lack of government action on decarbonisation. Academic John Ritzema called it a “massive overreach” and said the alert system should be “for ‘drop everything and prepare for something terrible’ situations”, something Coffey echoed, saying alerts should not become commonplace to avoid “Peter cries wolf situations”. Continue reading...

records.summary_source: ‘High coral cover is evidence of recovery and resilience, not evidence that the disturbances causing mortality didn’t happen,’ scientist says Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here The Australian newspaper appeared to think it had a slam-dunk this week with a front page story pointing to official government data which showed “the Great Barrier Reef is refusing to die” despite decades of warnings that global heating would cause its demise . In an editorial to back its reporting, the newspaper claimed the “continued good health” of the reef was a “welcome reminder that physics rather than the pseudo-religion of climate change doom still holds sway over the natural order.” Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 澳大利亚报纸根据官方数据在头版及社论中称大堡礁并未消亡，并指责气候变化预测是“伪宗教”。澳大利亚海洋科学研究所指出，该报报道存在过度简化的框架，高珊瑚覆盖率体现的是生态系统的恢复力与韧性，并不意味着气候变暖带来的长期风险已被夸大或科学共识失效。
records.why_zh: 该报道引发了关于媒体如何解读气候科学与生态监测数据的争论，凸显了公众舆论与科研机构在气候变化风险评估上的认识界限。

records.title_zh: 新研究显示亚马逊展现出令人惊叹的韧性，但临界点隐现
records.summary_source: - Three 2026 studies reveal that the Amazon can regrow quickly, but deforestation and warming could trigger a system-wide tipping point in the next 15 years. - Research also shows that repeated wildfires are replacing fire-resistant specialist trees with generalist species, halving biodiversity at forest edges despite a closing canopy. - According to research, extreme conditions have increased tree mortality due to hydraulic failure, which is key to understanding the forest’s shrinking carbon sinks. - Ending deforestation is necessary and achievable, but must be combined with global actions to curb climate change, say experts.
records.summary_zh: 2026年发布的三项研究表明，亚马逊雨林虽然在遭受极端事件后能快速恢复生长且对火灾表现出超预期韧性，但砍伐和变暖仍可能在未来15年内触发系统性临界点。极端条件导致的树木水分输送失效正加剧碳汇萎缩，专家指出停止森林砍伐必须与全球遏制气候变暖的行动相结合。

records.title_original: How can we talk about this extreme weather now that it’s a battleground in the culture wars? | Andy Beckett
records.title_zh: 既然极端天气已经成为文化战争的战场，我们该如何谈论它？| 安迪·贝克特
records.summary_source: Weather forecasts once gave Britons something safe to chat about. Not any more, and that’s a problem for the experts – indeed, for all of us In this fragmented but supposedly mild country, watching and talking about the weather forecast is meant to be a reassuring, unifying activity. Collectively, we have created and maintained a national climate narrative of small disappointments and pleasures. The first weather forecaster to appear on British TV, George Cowling, made his debut on the BBC in January 1954, predicting that “tomorrow would be rather windy”, but “a good day to hang out the washing”. For most of the 72 years since, such brief, carefully calibrated broadcasts have provided people from Aberdeen to Penzance with practical information, small talk and minor grumbles about essentially the same situation: living in a country where the weather is constantly changing, in a paradoxically unchanging way. Yet like the traditional British climate, that common weather culture may now be evaporating. “Met Office considers issuing red ‘extreme heat warning’ across Britain while nation enjoys ‘incredible summer’,” said the headline above the forecast on the GB News website on Monday, c

records.title_original: Fossils show huge carbon emissions harm forests, not ‘green the planet’
records.title_zh: 化石记录显示巨量碳排放会破坏森林而非“绿化地球”
records.summary_source: Study of 56m-year-old leaves counters claims from Trump administration members of ‘benefits’ of fossil fuel pollution Adding huge quantities of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere is set to cause the Earth’s forests to wither and die rather than flourish, according to a new study that counters erroneous claims that fossil fuel pollution will green the planet. An analysis of fossilized leaf cells from a period known as the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (or PETM), which occurred about 56m years ago, has helped reconstruct how the world’s forests responded when planet-heating gases were previously being released at a rapid rate. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 一项针对5600万年前古新世-始新世极热期化石叶片细胞的新研究显示，向大气中添加巨量二氧化碳会导致全球森林枯萎死亡而非繁盛。该研究反驳了化石燃料污染有益于地球的错误言论，并对当前空前快速的碳排放及其引发的生态崩塌敲响警钟。
records.why_zh: 提供了古气候学证据，反驳了碳排放有益论，对当前国际气候谈判中遏制森林退化与控制化石燃料具有重要科学与政策支撑意义。
records.poster_phrase: 碳排放破坏森林生态

records.title_original: Indonesia’s wildfire season surges as haze spreads into Malaysia
records.title_zh: 印尼野火季加剧，烟霾蔓延至马来西亚
records.summary_source: - Fires in Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province have sent haze across the border into Malaysia, where worsening air pollution has forced six schools in Sarawak state to switch to online classes. - Indonesia is entering the peak of its fire season, with West Kalimantan accounting for more than half of the nearly 49,000 hectares (121,000 acres) burned across six priority provinces as of Aug. 9. - The fires are also threatening biodiversity, including orangutan habitat and rehabilitation efforts in West Kalimantan, while a separate blaze has forced the closure of Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park on the island of Java. - Authorities have deployed tens of thousands of personnel and dozens of aircraft to fight the fires, but environmental groups say funding cuts and the intensifying El Niño are raising concerns about Indonesia’s preparedness.
records.summary_zh: 印度尼西亚西加里曼丹省的野火持续蔓延，产生的烟霾跨越国境飘散至马来西亚，导致马国砂拉越州空气污染加剧，多所学校被迫转为线上授课。印尼目前正进入野火高峰期，六个重点省份已有近4.9万公顷土地被烧毁，其中西加里曼丹省受灾最重，占总过火面积的一半以上。尽管当局已部署大量人员与装备灭火，但资金削减与厄尔尼诺现象加剧了外界对印尼防范能力的担忧。
records.why_zh: 反映了东南亚跨境野火对区域空气质量与公共健康的直接冲击，同时也暴露出极端气候与资金短缺对地方应急准备的压力。

records.title_original: ‘Everyone is scared’: flood-hit Porto Alegre braces for another El Niño
records.title_zh: “每个人都很害怕”：遭受洪水袭击的阿雷格里港正严阵以待应对又一次厄尔尼诺现象
records.summary_source: Two years after southern Brazil’s worst climate disaster ravaged the city, and with poor areas still recovering, many fear official neglect has left them exposed once again In the backstreets of Porto Alegre, a state capital in southern Brazil , you can still see signs of the devastating flood that swept through the city two years ago: scattered debris, waterlogged homes and destroyed businesses. In May 2024, flooding killed 183 people in the state of Rio Grande do Sul and displaced more than 600,000 . The neighbourhood of Sarandi was one of the hardest-hit parts of Porto Alegre , with water levels reaching up to 5 metres above normal, completely submerging many of its streets. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 在经历了两年前导致南里奥格兰德州183人死亡、超60万人流离失所的毁灭性洪水后，巴西南部阿雷格里港的贫困社区正面临新一轮厄尔尼诺现象带来的强降雨和洪水威胁。由于防洪设施不完善且政府搬迁计划滞后，当地居民担忧再次遭受忽视，凸显出气候危机下的环境与社会不公。
records.why_zh: 该报道揭示了极端气候灾害对发展中国家脆弱社区的不均衡冲击，凸显了地方防洪基础设施建设和政府适应政策滞后的现实风险。观点指出这构成气候正义危机，事实基于2024年洪灾数据及厄尔尼诺回归预测。

records.summary_zh: 生态环境部部长黄润秋于周四表示，截至2026年7月底，中国全国碳排放权交易市场累计成交量已超过9.3亿吨。该市场自2021年启动以来，有效降低了相关行业的减碳成本。未来，中国计划将全国碳市场覆盖范围进一步扩大至石化、化工等更多高排放行业，力争将全国约80%的二氧化碳排放纳入有效管控。
records.why_zh: 该数据表明中国碳市场在降低减碳成本方面取得实质成效，且未来扩大高排放行业覆盖范围的规划将进一步深化中国碳定价机制。

But with temperatures forecast to reach 36C or higher in parts of England on Thursday, the risk of further outbreaks remains high. Firefighters responded to 185 wildfires in the first 10 days of August. In coastal Suffolk, conservationists and locals are counting the cost of the blaze that devastated Dunwich Heath . Its vegetation and rare bird populations are expected to take decades to recover. You can read it in full here: There’s only one solution in the end to the drought now declared across most of England and that’s rain, says Hannah Cloke, professor of hydrology at the University of Reading. An important consequence of drought is that very dry soils can become less able to absorb rainfall when it does arrive. This can increase surface runoff and can even contribute to localised flash flooding, particularly if rain falls intensely over a short period. The current situation highlights the need to improve long-term resilience to both drought and flood risk as climate variability increases, and shows one more damaging impact of the burning of fossil fuels. records.title_original: Carbon markets alone won’t keep Southeast Asia’s forests standing, study says
records.title_zh: 全球碳治理议题受到关注
records.summary_source: - A new study has identified “massive and untapped” conservation potential within forestry and plantation concessions in Southeast Asia. - Roughly 42 million hectares of forests remain standing inside logging, oil palm, timber and rubber plantation concessions across the region, the study says. - The researchers examined what it would take to financially incentivize forest conservation inside these concessions, finding that using carbon markets alone would require carbon prices many times higher than current values. - They point to the need for diversified sources of conservation funding to complement carbon markets, such as blended finance, green bonds and payment for ecosystems services, as well as more supportive governance frameworks that elevate the viability of conservation over development.

records.summary_source: - Mining concessions have begun to encroach on protected areas and Indigenous and Afro-descendant territory, the result of a mining boom that began in 2022, according to a new investigation from community-based Indigenous group Wangki. - Since 1994, Nicaragua has granted 213 mining concessions covering more than 2.4 million hectares (5.9 million acres), representing approximately 20% of the country’s total land area. A significant portion of that — 113 of the concessions — has only been granted in the last three years. - The Nicaraguan government has signed trade agreements, passed new laws, and revised environmental regulations to help accelerate the expansion of the mining sector, especially by Chinese companies. - Pollution and deforestation from mining threaten ancestral traditions, and make it harder to practice subsistence farming and find clean drinking water, the investigation said.

records.summary_source: Matthew Wolfe’s Fires in the Night examines Earth Liberation Front, a US eco-anarchist movement, and its legacy of radical environmentalism Are echoes of 1990s radical environmentalism returning louder or fading away? It’s a question posed by Fires in the Night, a new book on the history of the Earth Liberation Front (ELF), a loosely grouped band of US Pacific north-west activists that used economic sabotage and arson to protest against environmental destruction. The members called themselves “the Family” and were known to the outside world as Elves, after the acronym for the group: ELF. Unlike rightwing extremists of the era, they practiced non-violence toward life, though not property. They were labelled domestic terrorists and practiced “leaderless resistance”. Continue reading...

records.title_original: Nutrients in our food are declining. Can regenerative agriculture save it?
records.title_zh: 农作物营养下降，能否靠再生农业挽救？
records.summary_source: Approach focuses on rebuilding soil health, increasing biodiversity and restoring natural ecosystems For the last few decades, the nutrient content of our crops has been declining. In the late 90s, the US Department of Agriculture found the vitamin C content of lemons had decreased by almost a third over the previous 22 years. Calcium in carrots, an important source especially for non-meat eaters, had reduced , on average, by more than a quarter. Vitamin A in bananas was down by 57%. The mineral content of wheat has declined by between 20-30% since the 1960s. A number of reasons have been suggested for this worrying decline, ranging from new varieties of crop that are bred to grow quicker and bigger to the higher carbon dioxide levels in the air causing plants to produce more sugars and starches (they grow faster but they produce fewer nutrients). A wide range of fixes have been suggested, from GM crops to synthetic soil amendments, or underground farms. Continue reading...

Observed for centuries in the Pacific by fishers, the El Niño weather phenomenon begins when the prevailing trade winds slow, allowing warm water to spread east along the coast of South America. records.summary_source: Sadiq Khan’s heat-ready plan for London is a sensible strategy for adaptation that should provide a roadmap for other cities “Our ability to trust that our homes will keep us safe from the outside is under threat,” the geographer Sam Johnson-Schlee writes in Hot House , his recent book on how heat has transformed domestic life. This summer, high temperatures have become inescapable. People have coped with makeshift solutions: keeping curtains drawn, placing foil over windows or – for those who can afford one – plugging in an air-conditioning unit. Planning experts warn that, with only about half of councils requiring new buildings to include cooling strategies, many homes will become “ death traps ” as temperatures rise. Britain’s homes weren’t built to cope with this. The country’s historically mild climate allowed developers to build houses without insulation, while industrialisation supplied plentiful coal to burn when temperatures dropped. Many homes are consequently draughty in winter and sweltering in summer. Unlike those in Mediterranean climates, British homes lack shutters and shaded communal spaces. records.title_zh: 气候危机加剧欧洲极端干旱
records.summary_source: Analysis shows how heatwaves are making atmosphere thirstier, damaging water supplies, food production and power generation Extreme heat supercharged by the climate crisis is sucking Europe dry in summer and intensifying the drought hitting the continent, a scientific analysis has found. Record-breaking heatwaves meant the hot atmosphere strongly evaporated water from rivers, lakes, soils and plants – conditions made 80 times more likely by global heating in western Europe and 40 times more likely in eastern Europe, the study showed. The level of soil dryness in the west was made five times more likely by the pollution from fossil fuels in the west, and 11 times more likely in the east. Continue reading...
records.summary_zh: 科学分析显示，气候危机导致极端高温，使欧洲大气“吸干”土壤水分，严重影响水资源、粮食生产和能源供应。西欧土壤干旱概率因化石燃料污染增加5倍，东欧则增加11倍。
records.why_zh: 极端高温和干旱加剧欧洲水资源和粮食安全风险，需加强气候适应和减排措施。事实基于科学分析。

records.title_original: Kemi declares war on net zero – and what remains of her party
records.title_zh: 英国保守党内部围绕净零政策的分裂加深
records.summary_source: Badenoch’s ideological purge gathers pace as moderates are cast out and the Tories edge ever closer to political extinction You have to hand it to Kemi Badenoch. She doesn’t take any prisoners. While the rest of us have been trying to survive a heatwave and are wondering if air-con may be needed for future summers, the Tory leader has taken a more hardline approach to climate change. Call it Schrödinger’s climate change. It’s both happening and not happening at the same time. Kemi is just about sane enough not to be an out-and-out denier. She leaves that to Reform. Mind you, no one would put it past her to suggest the scientists have got it wrong if the temperature drops for a few days. But her view is that while climate change may be real, there’s no point in trying to do anything about it. Continue reading...
